To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we proposed a novel reconstruction and analysis method for biomedical signals.

our proposed method yields better results than CS-based methods for reconstruction, and is capable of real time operation, and it is capable of yielding better results than traditional classification methods.

we propose a semi-supervised stacked label consistent autoencoder for reconstructing and classifiying biomedical signals, and it is faster than compressed sensing based methods and yields better results than traditional classification methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a holistic approach to signal processing that is capable of reconstructing and classifies the biomedical signals.
developing a new paradigm in signal processing that will be useful in many applications.
the reconstruction and analysis of biomedical signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is better than the existing methods for both reconstruction and classification.
the proposed method is capable of real time reconstruction and analysis of biomedical signals, and is a significant contribution to the field of signal processing.
the proposed method is capable of reconstructing and analyzing biomedical signals in real time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method is capable of reconstructing signals and analyzing them simultaneously, in a holistic fashion, without any assumption regarding the signals.
the reconstruction is learned and classification is done using the reconstruction itself, and the two are integrated into a unified framework.
we have proposed an autoencoder-based framework to simultaneously learn a signal representation and a linear classification map for signal reconstruction and analysis, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the representation learning framework can be applied to biomedical signal processing problems.
the reconstruction and classification can be performed in a holistic fashion, using an autoencoder.
reconstruction and analysis of biomedical signals should be treated as an integrated problem, and the solution to this problem should be “learned” using a data-driven approach.
